card.text: M43 is an H II region of the Orion Nebula complex about 414 parsecs away.

sources.label: Menten et al. (2007), The distance to the Orion Nebula, A&A 474, 515: 414 ± 7 pc from radio parallaxes of four stars in the Orion Nebula Cluster; M43 is part of the same nebula complex, so it takes the Orion Nebula's distance
Wikipedia, "Messier 43"
sources.quote: Messier 43 or M43, also known as De Mairan's Nebula and NGC 1982, is a star-forming nebula with a prominent H II region in the equatorial constellation of Orion.

introduction.text: NOIRLab's photograph of it stands here as a flat picture facing the Sun, 0.84 pc wide.

sources.label: NOIRLab noao-m43: N.A.Sharp/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA
sources.locator: M43, NGC 1982; a color composite; its page names no filters

sources.label: Wikipedia, "Messier 43"
sources.quote: It was discovered by the French scientist Jean-Jacques d'Ortous de Mairan some time before 1731, then catalogued by Charles Messier in 1769.

optical.title: M43 in visible light
optical.summary: A flat picture facing the Sun at the nebula's distance; nothing in it has depth.
